title: Framework Solids Possessing Both Hydrophobic and Hydrophilic Pores Constructed by Face-Sharing Keplerate-Type Heterometal–Organic Polyhedra

synthesis.procedure: An aqueous solution (10 mL) containing Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.58 g, 2.0 mmol) and trans-1,2-diaminocyclohexane-N,N,N′,N′-tetraacetic acid monohydrate (0.728 g, 2.0 mmol) was stirred at 80 °C. Its pH was adjusted to 6 with 1.0 M aqueous NaOH. The mixture was refluxed for 10 min, then 1.0 M aqueous La(ClO4)3 (2 mL) was added. The pH was readjusted to approximately 6 with 1.0 M aqueous NaOH, and the mixture was refluxed for 2 h. Filtration gave a deep-blue solution; crystals formed on standing under ambient conditions for two months.
synthesis.time: 10 min reflux before La addition; 2 h reflux afterward; two months for crystallization
synthesis.ph: 6 initially; readjusted to approximately 6 after La addition
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Aqueous reaction with stirring and reflux
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered; the deep-blue filtrate stood under ambient conditions for two months to yield crystals.

properties.summary: The susceptibility is consistent with paramagnetic behavior from 20 to 300 K. Its low-temperature decrease suggests very weak antiferromagnetic Ni–Ni coupling, potentially combined with zero-field splitting.

source_locations.location: Introduction and Experimental Section, synthesis of 1

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The three-dimensional framework is assembled by sharing square faces of La24[Ni(DCTA)]12 heterometal–organic cages. Each cage has an outer La24 rhombicuboctahedron enclosing an inner Ni12 cuboctahedron; an equivalent description uses [Ni(DCTA)]24La12 cages. The resulting framework contains hydrophobic pores lined by the DCTA cyclohexyl groups and hydrophilic pores lined by La-bound water.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared under the conditions specified for 1, replacing aqueous La(ClO4)3 with aqueous Gd(ClO4)3. An aqueous solution (10 mL) of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.58 g, 2.0 mmol) and trans-1,2-diaminocyclohexane-N,N,N′,N′-tetraacetic acid monohydrate (0.728 g, 2.0 mmol) was stirred at 80 °C and adjusted to pH 6 using 1.0 M aqueous NaOH. After 10 min of reflux, 1.0 M aqueous Gd(ClO4)3 (2 mL) was added; the pH was readjusted to approximately 6 and the mixture refluxed for 2 h. The shared procedure then specifies filtration and standing of the filtrate under ambient conditions for two months to crystallize the product.
synthesis.time: 10 min reflux before Gd addition; 2 h reflux afterward; two months for crystallization under the shared procedure
synthesis.ph: 6 initially; readjusted to approximately 6 after Gd addition
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Aqueous reaction with stirring and reflux
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered and left to crystallize under ambient conditions, following the procedure for 1.

properties.summary: The rise in χMT on cooling below approximately 30 K and the positive Curie–Weiss temperature are consistent with weak ferromagnetic Gd–Ni interactions.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The article identifies 2 as isostructural with the La analogue 1, differing in the numbers of coordinated and crystallization water molecules. Its three-dimensional framework is therefore described by face-sharing Keplerate-type Gd–Ni polyhedral cages, with outer rare-earth rhombicuboctahedral and inner Ni cuboctahedral arrangements and distinct hydrophobic and hydrophilic pores. The detailed cage analysis and figures are explicitly presented for 1 as the representative structure.
